body.p: I. Introduction

Claims 1-3 and 5-10 are pending in the present application. No new matter has been added. In view of the foregoing amendments and the following remarks, it is respectfully submitted that all the pending claims are allowable, and reconsideration is respectfully requested.
Applicant thanks the Examiner for the indication that claim 3 is allowable.
II. Rejection of Claim 5 Under 35 U.S.C. & 112

Claim 5 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112 as to definiteness. Claim 5 has been amended herein without prejudice, thereby rendering this rejection moot, and withdrawal of the definiteness rejection of claim 5 is therefore respectfully requested.
III. Rejection of Claims 1, 2, and 8-10 Under 35 U.S.C. & 103

Claims 1, 2, and 8-10 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as as unpatentable over the combination of U.S. Pat. App. Pub. Nos. 2020/0180605 ("Boecker") and 2018/0178769 ("Raste"). The combination of Boecker and Raste does not render unpatentable any of the present claims, and the rejection should be withdrawn, for at least the following reasons.

Independent claims 1, 9, and 10 refer to a steering direction towards a first target point and a setpoint direction towards a second target point, where, in response to a determined deviation of the steering direction from the setpoint direction, a transverse stabilization direction towards an entirely different third target point is set.

The Office Action asserts that Raste suggests to modify Boecker to provide this feature. Applicant respectfully disagrees. Boecker focuses on autonomous driving where a single desired trajectory is known and focuses on continuously correcting deviations from the pre- determined autonomous trajectory. The system uses sensor data to compare the vehicle's actual position and orientation to the desired trajectory. If there is a non-negligible significant deviation, corrective actions are taken. It does not involve a comparison between a driver's input and an ideal direction to trigger a completely separate corrective action. Boecker does not utilize a third target point separate from the desired trajectory and a driver input, and Boecker's corrective action is always towards the desired trajectory.

Raste does not correct this critical deficiency of Boecker and the Office's reliance on Raste is misplaced. Raste does not disclose a method where the system independently establishes a corrective steering direction, distinct from both the driver's actual steering direction and a setpoint direction. Instead, Raste focuses on inferring the driver's true intended direction by considering both steering wheel input and environmental factors. Raste's system uses

environmental cues (such as lane markings) to better understand what the driver is intending in the first place. The vehicle is then steered toward precisely the driver's inferred intended target point. There is no generation of a third, separate target point for corrective action. This is in contrast to the claims which specifically require setting a stabilization direction that differs from both the driver's input and the setpoint direction-a critical feature absent in Boecker and Raste.

Notwithstanding Applicant's disagreement with the rejection for the noted reasons, to facilitate matters, claims 1, 9, and 10 are amended herein without prejudice to include a feature related to the subject matter of claim 3, which has been indicated to be allowable, specifying a degree, relative to the steering direction, to which the setpoint direction factors into the setting of the transverse stabilization is dynamically adjusted depending on an extent of the deviation between the setpoint direction and the steering direction. The combination of Boecker and Raste does not disclose this feature.

The combination of Boecker and Raste therefore does not disclose or suggest all of the features of any of claim 1, 9, and 10, and therefore does not render unpatentable any of claims 1, 9, and 10, or either of claims 2 and 8, which depend from claim 1.
Withdrawal of the obviousness rejection of claims 1, 2, and 8-10 is therefore respectfully requested.
IV. Rejection of Claim 5 Under 35 U.S.C. & 103

Claim 5 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as unpatentable over the combination of Boecker, Raste, and WO 2020/157798 ("Utsui"). Claim 5 depends from claim 1 and is therefore allowable for at least the same reasons as claim 1 because Utsui does not correct the critical deficiencies of Boecker and Raste noted above as to claim 1. Withdrawal of the obviousness rejection of claim 5 is therefore respectfully requested.
V. Rejection of Claims 6 and 7 Under 35 U.S.C. 4 103

Claims 6 and 7 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as unpatentable over the combination of Boecker, Raste, and U.S. Pat. App. Pub. No. 2022/0281525 ("Ost"). Claims 6 and 7 depend from claim 1 and are therefore allowable for at least the same reasons as claim 1 because Ost does not correct the critical deficiencies of Boecker and Raste noted above as to claim 1. Withdrawal of the obviousness rejection of claims 6 and 7 is therefore respectfully requested.
VI. Conclusion

All issues raised having been addressed, it is therefore respectfully requested that the rejections be withdrawn. Prompt reconsideration and allowance of the present application are therefore earnestly solicited.
